newsitem.title: USA: Firefighters more optimistic about Calif. blaze.
newsitem.headline: Firefighters more optimistic about Calif. blaze.

text.p: Firefighters were more optimistic Sunday about holding back a wildfire that has burned for nine days in a scenic area near the central California coast.
"Things are looking good," Cece Stewart, a spokeswoman for the U.S. Forest Service, said about the fire burning in the Ventana wilderness area near Big Sur, 150 miles south of San Francisco.
The 4,400-acre fire was not advancing, she said. It was only 35 percent contained but firefighters for the first time estimated that the blaze would be fully contained by Nov 2.

Some 2,700 firefighters were battling the blaze, burning in rugged, inaccessible forest and brush. Hand crews were building fire lines around the fire Sunday while air tankers and helicopters were dropping fire retardant and water on the blaze.

Fire officials had feared that winds would whip up on each of the last two days, which could have pushed the fire towards the town of Big Sur. Residents of the town were put on alert Saturday to be ready to evacuate.
But Stewart said the winds had failed to materialize for the last two days, although strong winds were again forecast for later Sunday.
She said no property was threatened by the fire unless winds blow to the south. The Ventana wilderness area has been closed to hikers as a precaution, she said.
Officials estimated the cost of the firefighting effort at nearly $4.8 million so far and said it could reach $9.8 million. The cause of the fire is under investigation.
